findings.F1: Weekend rises are not reversed over Monday and Tuesday. Across 1124 cases the unusual move is −0.02 % (t −0.10) and the total move is −0.29 % against a trade cost of 0.19 %. The slope of the next 48 hours on the weekend's 48-hour return is −0.036 (t −1.21, n 1932). By weekend z-quintile, the next 48 hours rise most after the largest weekend falls (+0.51 %) and after the largest weekend rises (+0.64 %), so no quintile shows a reversal.
findings.F2: The book loses by shorting against the coins' rise. Its mean daily return is −0.023 % while holding the coins earns +0.119 % a day. The book is short on 25 % of bars (mean position −0.08). Its 2161 trades lose 1.16 % each before fees and 1.26 % after, win 27 % of the time, and last about 61 hours.
findings.F3: When a coin's 30-day hourly volatility is low against its own 6-month volatility, the weekend move continues over Monday and Tuesday instead of reversing. The continuation's unusual move is +0.97 % (t 2.49, 457 cases, strength 0.14) and its total move is +1.00 %, about 5 times the 0.19 % cost. In the middle and hot thirds of that ratio the continuation is −0.15 % and −0.05 % (t −0.50 and −0.16).
findings.F4: Inside that calm regime the continuation is strongest after weekend falls and after the largest weekend moves:
findings.F5: The same pattern shows on the coin's own volatility thirds. In each coin's lowest-volatility third, the slope of the next 48 hours on the standardised weekend move is +0.0101 (t 3.55, n 645) and the reversal is −0.50 % (t −2.27). In the highest third the reversal is +0.15 % (t 0.40). There, the reversal grows with the weekend move's size from −1.10 % to +1.11 % across quartiles (top-quartile strength 0.16), but after weekend rises it is only +0.50 % (t 1.00, n 332).

ideas.idea: When a coin's 30-day hourly volatility is low against its own last 6 months, its move from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC continues in the same direction over the following two days (Monday and Tuesday). The larger the weekend move, the larger the continuation.
ideas.consequence: In calm weeks a trader would follow the weekend's direction into Monday and Tuesday rather than fade it, and would refuse the weekend fade in those weeks.
ideas.name: calm-regime weekend move continues

ideas.idea: When a coin's price rises from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC, it falls over the following two days (Monday and Tuesday), only while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its own last 6 months. The larger the weekend gain, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade a weekend rise only in turbulent weeks, and stand aside from the fade in calm ones, where the move tends to carry on instead.
ideas.name: weekend reversal in turbulent weeks
